newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move sideways in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move sideways in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks eased in early Friday morning trade, but the decline was subdued due partly to investors focus on second liners and China plays, brokers said.
"Hopefully Wall Street's impact is being diluted by the greater exposure (of the market) to the China concept, said one local broker. "People are focusing on second and third liners and red chips."
The Hang Seng Index was down 24 points at 13,178 in early trade on relatively robust volume of HK$1.77 billion.
The broad market was more stable, with the All Ordinaries Index showing a drop of only 2.66 points to 6,464.87.

On Thursday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 5.78 points down at 6,442.49, after recovering from an 96-point intraday plunge. The fall was precipitated by a drop in the bond market following news of stronger-than-expected U.S. manufacturing activity in November.
But the dip in the U.S. long bond of 1-6/32 to 96-30/32, to yield 6.74 percent, was minor and brokers said there would be good interest at the 6.75 percent level.
The H share index of 23 Chinese state enterprises advanced 2.59 percent in the first 30 minutes of trade.

Qingling Motors led the sector with a gain of HK$0.325 to HK$4.925. Guangdong Kelon added HK$0.30 to HK$5.90, a record high. The company announced a new joint venture which would give the company greater distribution of its current and new lines of refrigerators throughout China.

In the blue chip sector, the commercial and industrial index led the market down, chiefly on profit-taking in CITIC Pacific. The share was dropped to a low of HK$43.80, then rebounded to trade down HK$0.90 at HK$44.20.
In the mid-cap sector, Wing Hang Bank advanced HK$0.20 to HK$35.60, while Dah Sing lost HK$0.30 to HK$30.90.
Red chip COSCO Pacific gained HK$0.30 to HK9.15 and C.P. Pokphand put on HK$0.20 to HK$3.20. Guangzhou Investment rose HK$0.15 to HK$3.90.
China Resources was one of the most active, easing HK$0.05 to HK$18.05 to HK$173.67 million.
